pages.title: Farmer's Delight
pages.text: Farmer's Delight is a farming and cooking overhaul that adds crops, cooking tools, and a wide variety of prepared meals. Its biggest impact on Nourished is that many of its cooked dishes cover $(bold)multiple food groups at once$(), making them incredibly efficient for maintaining all six bars.

pages.title: New Crops
pages.text:
Farmer's Delight adds several new crops that slot into existing groups:

$(bold)Tomato$() — Vegetables; fast-growing and versatile.
$(bold)Onion$() — Vegetables; distinct allium family.
$(bold)Rice$() — Grains; introduces a new grain family separate from wheat.
$(bold)Cabbage$() — Vegetables; leafy green family.
$(bold)Beetroot Seeds$() (improved) — better yield than vanilla beetroot.

pages.title: Cooked Meals
pages.text:
Farmer's Delight meals are where Nourished integration shines. Many dishes cover two or three groups in one item:

$(bold)Stew / Soup$() — typically Vegetables + Grains.
$(bold)Roast Chicken$() — Proteins + Vegetables.
$(bold)Bacon and Eggs$() — Proteins + Dairy.
$(bold)Rice Bowl$() — Grains + Vegetables.
$(bold)Stuffed Pumpkin$() — Grains + Vegetables + Proteins.

pages.title: Cooking Pot
pages.text:
The $(bold)Cooking Pot$() is Farmer's Delight's crafting station for meals. Investing in one early pays off immediately for Nourished — cooking a pot of stew that covers three groups is far more inventory-efficient than carrying separate foods for each.

Prioritize recipes that cover your weakest groups. Check the tooltip of any cooked meal to see which Nourished groups it contributes to.

pages.title: Rotation Advice
pages.text:
Farmer's Delight meals each have their own food family, so rotating between different dishes avoids diminishing returns even when multiple dishes share a group.

A good daily rotation might be: $(bold)Roast Chicken$() for lunch (Proteins + Veg), $(bold)Rice Bowl$() for dinner (Grains + Veg), and a dairy item when needed. Three meals can cover every group with zero repetition.
